Vehicles by geofence

The number in each ring = all vehicles there now (standing + moving + offline), so all cards together add up to the whole fleet. "No geofence" = every vehicle outside all geofences, including vehicles on the road and vehicles without a location. Each vehicle is counted in one card only (if geofences overlap, loading/unloading wins, then the nearest). Click a card for km run and engine hours of those vehicles in the last 3, 7, 12 hours and yesterday.

Calls to make (0)

Timeline period
Route stop: vehicle stopped outside plant, queue and mine for more than the route limit. Call the driver or supervisor. Loading delay: vehicle inside a mine (Loading geofence) longer than the loading limit. Call that mine's loading manager (the in-charge saved on the geofence in Places and people). Unloading delay: inside the unloading point or its queue longer than the unloading limit. After a call, the case stays "Called" until the follow-up time passes; if the vehicle is still standing it comes back as "Follow-up due". Limits are in Settings.

Call report · calls needed vs done

Every alert in the period that needed a call, rebuilt from the timeline with the current limits (route stop, loading, unloading). A call counts if it was logged for that vehicle while it was standing (or within 1 hour after it moved). "Missed" = no call logged. Response time = from the moment the alert started until the first call.

Map and direction

Draw a circle, rectangle or polygon with the tools on the left of the map to create a geofence. Use the edit (pencil) tool to change an existing shape. Trails are shown only for moving vehicles or vehicles that moved more than 1 km. Direction is based on whether the distance to the plant went down or up over the last ~10 minutes.

Recommended geofences

Where your tippers really load and unload, found from the data — and which geofence to make there. Loading = tippers stand next to an excavator again and again. Unloading = where tippers stop right after being loaded (dump point / hopper / stockpile). With these geofences you get full trips: trip time, km and the Cycle time breakdown. Press + Create, check the circle on the satellite map, then Save.

When a vehicle's GPS sends no signal for the hours set in a level below, one email per site and level goes to that site's contacts, listing the vehicles and asking to mark Breakdown or repair the GPS. Geofence to geofence trips

A trip starts when the vehicle leaves the From geofence (last reading inside) and ends when it next reaches the To geofence (first reading inside). If it goes back into From first, the trip restarts from there. When From and To are the same, it shows how long and how many km the vehicle took to come back to that geofence. km = GPS km between the two readings; stops on the way = stopped or idling on the road. Very short hops (under 10 min and under 0.3 km, GPS jumping at the edge) are left out. Geofences drawn later count for past data only after select public.rebuild_segments(48);.

Loading pairs · tipper ↔ excavator

A loading is counted when a tipper stands (stopped or idling) for at least two readings next to an excavator or loader whose engine is on. The excavator's position is the median of its last 20 minutes, so GPS jumps do not move it. When two excavators are close, the nearer one gets the loading. For the first 7 days every excavator uses 50 m; after that its radius is set automatically to the distance within which 90% of its loadings happened (admin can override below).

Loading rules and learning

A tipper's next loading counts only when it has travelled at least the minimum trip km since its previous counted loading. A shorter visit is the same trip: it is not counted again and its km are carried into the next trip. A loading also needs the tipper to stand next to the loader for at least the minimum loading time. The tables show how the real data of the last 14 days is spread, so these limits can be tuned. Suggested values appear once there are 30+ real trips.

Radius learning

P50 / P90 = distance within which half / 90% of the excavator's loadings (last 7 days) happened. Learned radius is set once a day after 7 days and at least 15 loadings, between 15 m and the learning radius. A manual value (admin) always wins; clear it to go back to automatic.
ExcavatorStatusLoadings (7 days, updated daily)P50P90LearnedIn useManual (admin)

Machine utilization

Machines are the vehicle types listed in Settings (Excavator, Loader, Roller…). Engine on = engine running (a machine working in one place at under 3 km/h counts as engine on). Running = time spent moving. Machine efficiency = Engine on ÷ total time passed in the selected period × 100 (Today: hours passed since 12:00 AM; Yesterday: 24 hours; 7 days: the last 168 hours). Off = engine off; No signal = GPS not sending. Time is counted from the 2-minute readings, so gaps when the poller was down are left out. Loadings come from the Loading pairs page.
